classifiedFinding.title: setDispatcherHook rotation orphans the old hook's outstanding mintDebt, leaving rewardBudget stale and DoSing reward claims until corrective action

classification.assetImpact: Reward-claim DoS between a hook rotation and the next owner corrective action (topUp, rotate back, or admin pull on a still-callable old hook). Stakers forced onto emergencyWithdraw forfeit pending rewards. No principal theft; no direct external-attacker path — the failure is gated entirely on owner action (rotating to a hook with mintDebt < the old hook's outstanding ledger).
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setDispatcherHook(newHook), where oldHook had mintDebt = M > 0 unrealised.
2. setDispatcherHook overwrites the reference without calling _syncBudget (no pull on oldHook) or _recomputeSchedule (no refresh against newHook). M is now orphaned.
3. The prior _recomputeSchedule had set rewardBudget = V - committedDebt with V including M. Stakers continue accruing against an inflated rewardBudget.
4. Subsequent _updatePool calls drain rewardBudget at the rate sized for the inflated V; committedDebt grows against value the contract no longer expects to receive.

5. A claim eventually hits _safePay with balance < pending; reverts with 'insufficient reward balance'. Recovery requires owner topUp, rotating back to oldHook (if still functional), or installing a hook with sufficient mintDebt to cover the gap.
classification.likelihood: n/a - centralization risk; failure mode requires owner action (hook rotation) and is not externally triggerable.
classification.assumptions: Owner rotates to a hook whose mintDebt at the time of rotation is materially less than the orphaned mintDebt on the old hook.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner action; documented as a 'live operation' per CLAUDE.md item 7 but the spec does not require draining the old hook before rotation.

classifiedFinding.justification: Centralization. The failure is gated on owner action — specifically, an owner mistake during hook rotation (failing to drain the old hook first or top up the contract afterwards). No external attacker can trigger this state; the dispatcher hook is owner-set and in the same trust domain. Reclassified from Medium (per prior runs) to Centralization on re-evaluation: per C4 Regular Audit guidance, 'Mistakes unblocked by admin -> QA Report' and 'Privilege escalation -> Judge by likelihood and impact'. This is a footgun affecting a privileged path with no external-attacker vector — properly a Centralization-class finding even though the failure mode resembles a Medium availability impact, because the predicate (owner rotates without draining) is purely admin-driven. The recommendation (call _syncBudget before and _recomputeSchedule after, mirroring sister setters) is a low-cost defensive improvement.
